title: Pad see ew
summary: Wide rice noodles wok-tossed with Chinese broccoli, egg and savoury dark soy until lightly charred.
method: Separate the noodles gently. Slice the chicken thinly and cut the Chinese broccoli stems and leaves separately.
Mix the light and dark soy sauces with the oyster sauce.
Heat the oil in a wok on high until smoking. Sear the chicken until cooked through, with no pink remaining.
Add the broccoli stems, then the leaves, and cook for 1 minute until the leaves are bright green and just wilted.
Push everything aside and scramble the eggs until just set. Add the noodles and sauce and toss on high for 2 minutes.
Let the noodles sit against the wok for 30 seconds until the edges char, then serve hot.

stages.title: Build the flavours
steps: Mix soy sauces and oyster sauce
heat oil in wok until smoking and sear chicken until cooked through.

stages.title: Cook the dish
steps: Add broccoli stems, then leaves, and cook for 1 minute until the leaves are bright green
push aside, scramble eggs, add noodles and sauce and toss on high heat for 2 minutes.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Let noodles sit briefly against wok for charred edges, then serve hot.

tips: Cook in batches if wok is small to avoid steaming noodles.
variations: Swap chicken for firm tofu and vegetarian stir-fry sauce.
storage: Refrigerate 2 days; reheat thoroughly in a hot pan.

title: Pain perdu
summary: Thick slices of day-old brioche soaked in vanilla custard and pan-fried until golden and soft inside.
method: Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar and vanilla in a shallow dish. Heat a large frying pan over medium heat.
Soak the brioche slices for 20–30 seconds per side, until the custard soaks in but the slices hold together.
Melt the butter in the pan, then cook the slices in batches for 3–4 minutes per side, until golden and the centre is set.
Serve straight away with the berries and a light dusting of icing sugar, if using.
